top_choice_rationale: P003 rests on a concrete, measured chemistry: a 3'-O-blocked, fluorescently labelled reversible terminator incorporated by an engineered polymerase, cleanly unblocked on a surface, plus single-molecule arrays. This turned DNA copying into a cycle-by-cycle chemical readout and drove the fall in genome cost. It is mature, independently reproduced and widely deployed, and the two-name cut matches the decisive steps. The main weakness is that sequencing may be seen as genomics technology, and Mayer, Ju and Rothberg are left out. I rank P001 second because the Vancouver trio now gives the clean ionizable-lipid and rapid-mixing story I said I would support.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my own research depends on sequencing and nucleotide measurements, which may bias me toward P003, but I know none of the credited persons
